item.title: Bitcoin testing a key support target. What needs to happen to give buyers some relief?
item.description:
Bitcoin moved higher with stocks in the risk-on trade that followed the election results. Yesterday, that trade went into reverse. As AI concerns sent stocks tumbling, Bitcoin gave up its post-election gains, fell back below its 100-day moving average and returned to a swing area that has repeatedly come into play since August.

In the video above, I walk through the chart and outline what needs to happen to give buyers some relief. Where can buyers lean with close risk? What levels would they need to get above to take back some control? And where does the price have room to roam if the floor gives way?

The swing area is the immediate barometer.

Bitcoin was trading near $75,632 at the time of the chart, inside the swing area between $74,925 and $76,052. The upper end is the 38.2% retracement of the move up from the July low. The lower end is the floor buyers need to defend.

As long as the price holds above $74,925, buyers have a level to lean against with close risk. The first sign of relief would be a move back above $76,052 that can hold. That would take the price out of the swing area and give buyers a shot at the next upside target.

The moving averages are the next hurdles.

The 100-day moving average comes in at $77,061. Get above that and stay above, and traders can start to eye the 100-hour and 200-hour moving averages at $77,631 and $77,795, respectively. Those two hourly averages are close enough to treat as a zone. A move through both would give buyers more confidence and open the door to the next swing level near $79,146.

Until the price starts reclaiming those levels, sellers still have the technical edge.

A break of the floor would give sellers more room.

Move below $74,925 and stay below, and the focus shifts to the 200-day moving average at $73,190. Below that, the next target is the 50% midpoint of the move up from the July low at $72,554.

The distinction I’m watching is what happens after a break. A dip below $74,925 that quickly moves back into the swing area would put sellers on alert for a failed break. A break that stays below the floor, especially if a bounce stalls back near $74,925, would show that sellers are starting to lean against the old support. That’s the price action that would put the lower targets in play.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: Iran reviewing proposals to curb nuclear program - report
item.description:
Iranian negotiators are reviewing proposals that would see Tehran curb its nuclear program, according to the Times of Israel.

Iran had previously refused to put the issue on the table until its seven conditions were met. Now there appears to be a thawing on that stance, if the reporting is correct. It cites a US official and a diplomat familiar.

"The proposals stop short of complete dismantlement, but do address Iran’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium, the diplomat familiar with the talks adds, saying that the offers would see Iran receive significant sanctions relief from the US."

WTI crude is down 18-cents today to $90.33 but has fallen dramatically this week on hopes for a peace deal after the Iran war proved wildly unpopular at the ballot box.

item.title: Broader US stock indices bounce higher but still has work to do to give buyers more hope
item.description:
The S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite and Nasdaq 100 are bouncing, but buyers still have key technical levels to reclaim.

Yesterday’s selloff left the major US stock indices in a deep hole. The Nasdaq 100 fell 6.36%, its biggest one-day decline since 2020, and the weakness spread well beyond the tech-heavy index. Along the way, the selling broke technical levels that buyers had leaned against. Those breaks matter today because some of the same levels that gave way on the way down are now the first hurdles on the climb back.

Today, the major indices are finding their footing. The bounce is welcome, but there is still work to do before buyers can start to wrestle back more control. The first test is what happens when the rebound reaches a level that broke yesterday. Can buyers get above it and stay above it? If they can, the next upside target comes into focus. If the rally stalls and sellers lean against that old support, yesterday’s lows can come back into play.

In the video above, I walk through the S&P 500, the Nasdaq Composite and the Nasdaq 100 one at a time. I look at what each index broke on the way down, what today’s rebound has managed to repair and where the next test comes in. Which levels would give buyers more confidence if reclaimed? Where can buyers define close risk if they step in? And what would tell us that sellers are taking control again?

Dips have often found buyers, but the climb back can take longer than the fall. After a day like yesterday, traders have to sort through the fundamental stories, shifts in positioning and a change in the market’s appetite for risk. All of that goes into the witches’ brew that drives price action. In the meantime, the chart gives traders something concrete to work with. A broken swing area or moving average can become a barometer for the bias. If buyers reclaim it and hold it on a pullback, they have a level to lean against and a target to look toward. If the level gives way again, they know where the case for the rebound starts to weaken.

For now, buyers have taken the first step out of the hole. How they handle the levels that gave way yesterday will tell us how much further the rebound can go.

A look at the charts

Watch the video for the your roadmap but below is a look at the charts for the S&P, Nasdaq composite and Nasdaq 100 indices:

S&P Index: 

The S&P index stalled the fall ahead of the 200 day MA at 7325 and a swing area down to 7300. If that level can hold, the upside target at 7507 is the target for buyers followed by the 100 day MA at 7619.  

Nasdaq Composite Index.  

The low yesterday did stall in the swing area between 24206 and 24425. The price today is above that area but below the 200 day MA at 25098 and the broken 38.2% at 25036. Get above each is needed to increase the bullish bias.  

Nasdaq 100. 

The fall in the Nasdaq 100 is seeing a rebound, but the move back above the broken 50% is failing (at 27103). If the buyers are to scare the sellers (or the buyers to gain confidence), they need to get and stay above 27103. 

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: November US UMich prelim consumer sentiment 51.0 vs 48.0 expected
item.description:
• Prior was 46.3
  • Current conditions 51.0 vs 48.0 expected
  • Expectations 50.9 vs 49.5 expected
  • One-year inflation 4.3 vs 4.7% prior
  • Five-year inflation 3.4 vs 3.5% prior

The University of Michigan’s Surveys of Consumers is one of the oldest measures of US household sentiment but it's lost its lustre in financial markets due to readings that don't correspond with spending. The preliminary reading is released at 10 am ET in the first half of each month, based on interviews conducted over the preceding weeks. A final reading incorporating the full sample follows near the end of the month. The preliminary figure sometimes draws a market reaction because it’s the first look at the month.

The headline Index of Consumer Sentiment is built from questions about personal finances, business conditions and whether it’s a good time to buy big-ticket items. It’s indexed to 100 in early 1966. The survey splits into two sub-indexes, current economic conditions and consumer expectations. The expectations measure is a component of the Conference Board’s Leading Economic Index.

Inflation expectations are lately the most market-sensitive part of the release and the Fed will be pleased with the dip in today's report. Respondents estimate price changes over the next year and over the next five to 10 years. The Federal Reserve watches the longer-run measure as a signal of whether inflation expectations remain anchored, and sharp moves can shift Treasury yields and rate pricing. Because the preliminary sample is smaller, these figures can be revised meaningfully in the final release.

The survey moved from telephone to online interviews in 2024, complicating comparisons with its long history. Responses have also become increasingly partisan, with sentiment swinging sharply depending on which party controls the White House.

Sentiment readings don’t always match spending, and households often keep buying even when they say they’re pessimistic. Still, the survey provides a timely read on how consumers are reacting to inflation, tariffs, gasoline prices, the job market and stock prices. I'd argue they were a good indicator of what was coming in the midterms, rather than what is/was coming in the economy.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: USD moves higher after the US jobs report. What levels are in play now?
item.description:
The US dollar moved higher after the October jobs report came in stronger than expected. Nonfarm payrolls rose 165K versus the 65K estimate, September was revised up to 60K from 29K, and the net revision over the prior two months was +84K. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%, even as labor force participation ticked higher.

The wage numbers also got the market’s attention. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% from a year ago, both above expectations. There was some softness beneath the headline, with the U6 underemployment rate rising to 7.9% from 7.6% as more people worked part time for economic reasons. Still, the combination of stronger payrolls and firmer wages put a potential December Fed hike more in play. The US 2-year yield rose 4.5 basis points on the day to 4.52%, while USDJPY was up 72 pips at 158.38 in the initial report.

Can the dollar hold its gains?

In the video above, I go through EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, USDCHF, USDCAD and AUDUSD. For each pair, I identify the level that acts as a barometer for buyers and sellers, where traders can define close risk, and the next targets if the move continues.

The first move after payrolls can come quickly. What I want to see next is whether the price can stay beyond the levels it broke. For USDJPY, USDCHF and USDCAD, that means seeing whether buyers can hold above broken resistance. For EURUSD, GBPUSD and AUDUSD, it means seeing whether sellers can keep the price below broken support. If those breaks hold, traders have a level to lean against as they look toward the next target. If the price moves back through the breakout level, that’s the first clue the post-jobs move is losing momentum.

EURUSD: The EURUSD is below a swing area between 1.1152 to 1.1160. Stay below and the lows from October are targeted. 

USDJPY: The USDJPY is moving back to the 200 day MA at 158.60.  Like I have been saying for a while, get and stay above that MA is needed to give the buyers more control. Buyers have tried going back to September, but buyers turn to sellers. The price moved above the 200 and 100 hour MA at 157.93 and 158.104. That is a risk level now.

GBPUSD: The GBPUSD fell and ran from the 100 day MA and the 200 hour MA at 1.3392. Stay below keeps the sellers in control. The broken 38.2% at 1.3342 is the next target.

  

USDCHF: The USDCHF is trading higher and tests the 200 hour MA and broken 38.2% near 0.8224. Get above would be more bullish. Stay below and the price is between the 100 hour MA at 0.8172.  

USDCAD: The USDCAD has the stronger US and the weaker Canada jobs to digest. That has the price moving higher and into the swing area between 1.4129 and 1.4153.  

AUDUSD: The AUDUSD is testing the  key swing area floor going back to January. That area comes between 0.6832 up to 0.6863.  

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: US October non-farm payrolls +165K vs +65K expected
item.description:
• Prior was +29K (revised to +60K)
  • Two-month net revision +84K
  • Unemployment rate 4.1% vs 4.2% expected
  • Prior unemployment rate 4.2%
  • Unrounded unemployment 4.141% vs 4.1753% prior
  • Participation rate 61.9% vs 61.8% prior
  • U6 underemployment rate 7.9% vs 7.6% prior
  • Average hourly earnings +0.4% m/m vs +0.3% expected
  • Average hourly earnings 3.1% y/y vs +2.9% expected
  • Average weekly hours 34.4 vs 34.4 expected
  • Change in private payrolls +159K vs +64K expected
  • Prior private payrolls +46K (revised to +78K)
  • Change in manufacturing payrolls 19K vs +5K expected
  • Government payrolls +6K vs -17K prior
  • Household survey +463K

This is a beat from bottom to top and the wage growth will certainly make the Fed look twice. They will get another jobs report before the December 9 FOMC but this one will certainly make it more likely that they will hike rates.

If there is a hint of weakness in the report is the rise in U6. Part-time for economic reasons rose +339k to 4.84M. Almost all of it came from “slack work or business conditions” (+356k). That’s employers cutting hours.

US 2-year yields are up 4.5 bps on the day to 4.52% and USD/JPY is up 72 pips to 158.38. S&P 500 futures are still slightly higher but I think the stock market is focused on things other than macro at the moment.

Note that last month was a soft one across the board so there isn't necessarily momentum here but there are no real signs of weakness, especially considering that most of the pre-NFP jobs data was also strong for October.

Another interesting point is that there is a bifurcation in the construction center between data centers and everything else. Nonresidential specialty trade contractors are +101k y/y. Residential specialty contractors are -36k y/y, including -15.2k in October alone. Higher rates won't help unwind that.

This article was written by Adam Button at investinglive.com.

item.title: Canada Employment change for October -4.7K vs 13.6K estimate. Unemployment rate 6.7%.
item.description:
• Prior month -68.3K

Details:

  • Employment change −4,700 vs +13,600 expected. Prior −68,000.

  • Unemployment rate 6.7% vs 6.5% expected. Prior 6.5%.

  • Employment rate 60.5% vs 60.6% in September.

  • Average hourly wages +2.2% year over year vs +2.3% in September, before seasonal adjustment.

  • Full time employment -18.1K vs -35.4K last month

  • Part Time employment 13.4K v -32.9k last month 

October components compared with September

  • Youth unemployment 13.7% vs 13.0%.

  • Unemployment among people aged 55 and older 5.5% vs 5.3%.

  • Educational services employment +15,000 vs −35,000.

  • Alberta employment −24,000 vs +23,000.

  • British Columbia employment +12,000 vs −20,000.

Canada’s October jobs report came in weaker than expected on both headline measures. Statistics Canada reported that employment was little changed, down 4,700 after declines of 68,000 in September and 42,000 in August. The unemployment rate rose to 6.7% as 33,000 more people looked for work.

The private sector was the soft spot. Private-sector employment fell 53,000, its first decline since February, while public-sector employment rose 50,000. Wholesale and retail trade lost 29,000 jobs, while construction added 16,000 and educational services added 15,000.

Here is the graphic of where the jobs were gained and lossed:

Quick analysis

The private-sector decline and slower wage growth give the Bank of Canada a reason to be cautious about another hike after it raised its policy rate to 2.50% in October. The offset is energy-driven inflation. The Bank raised rates because it was concerned that higher energy costs would spread to other prices. On its own, the jobs miss would normally weigh on the Canadian dollar and short-term Canadian yields, putting upward pressure on USDCAD.

The USDCAD moves higher

The combination of the stronger US jobs report and the Canada weaker look, has pushed the USDCAD to a new high for the day and going back to October 20. The price has also moved above a swing area target between 1.4068 to 1.40828 (inclusive of the borken 38.2%).  The next target? 1.4110.  

What this report measures

Statistics Canada’s monthly Labour Force Survey estimates how many people are employed and what share of the labour force is unemployed. The headline employment and unemployment figures are seasonally adjusted to make month-to-month comparisons easier. Traders watch the report for signs of labour-market slack and wage pressure that could influence Bank of Canada policy.

This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

item.title: BoE's Pill: No repeat of 2022 hiking cycle as growth risks could keep rates on hold
item.description:
• Limited evidence of second-round effects
  • Decision to raise rates preemptive in nature
  • Activity and employment adding to demand at the margin
  • Pipeline pressure in system from energy prices
  • We are not going to repeat 2022 rate hiking cycle
  • Nothing baked in for interest rates next year, outlook becomes more uncertain from Spring
  • It's possible that the bank rate would stay on hold or even fall if we saw stalling of growth next year
  • Key determinant will be the margin squeeze on companies and how companies react
  • We are putting weight on pay bargaining, costs, pricing

Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill reiterated that there is still limited evidence of second-round effects from higher energy prices. He stressed that the recent decision to raise interest rates was pre-emptive in nature, aimed at containing inflationary pressures before they become more persistent.

Pill acknowledged that there were different views within the MPC. While activity and employment are still adding to demand at the margin, higher energy prices are creating pipeline inflationary pressures that the Bank needs to monitor.

He stressed that the BoE is not planning to repeat the aggressive rate hiking cycle seen in 2022. He also pushed back against expectations for a predetermined policy path, saying nothing is baked in for interest rates next year and that the outlook is likely to become more uncertain from the spring. Importantly, Pill said that rates could remain on hold or even fall next year if economic growth were to stall. This is a rather dovish comment from a hawkish member.

Pill stressed that the BoE is trying to contain the risk of energy-driven inflation becoming entrenched without committing to an extended tightening cycle. More rate hikes will depend heavily on whether inflation pressures broaden and whether the economy can withstand the squeeze on businesses and households.

The market is currently pricing in a 50% chance of a rate hike in December and a total of 68 bps of tightening by the end of 2027. A lot will depend on the US-Iran developments and the incoming economic data.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: Morning Kickstart | Nasdaq futures rebound after rout as U.S. and Canadian jobs reports loom

Currency ranges ahead of the data

Stronger U.S. data and weaker Canadian data would favor the upside, while the reverse would favor the downside.

Stocks, yields and commodities

North American calendar

Unemployment is expected to hold at 4.2%. Average hourly earnings are forecast to rise 0.3% on the month after 0.1%, with annual growth easing to 2.9% from 3.0%. The average workweek is expected to hold at 34.4 hours.

Last month’s losses were split between full-time jobs (−35.4K) and part-time jobs (−32.9K). I’ll watch whether full-time employment participates in any rebound.

For the U.S. report, I’ll look at revisions and wages alongside the payroll headline. A payroll beat accompanied by softer wages could get a different reaction in yields than a beat with hotter earnings. That distinction matters for the dollar and for a Nasdaq trying to recover from yesterday’s selloff.

In the morning video above, I take a look at the three major currency pairs—EURUSD, USDJPY and GBPUSD—from a technical perspective. For each pair, I outline the bias, the risk-defining levels and the targets that would give either the buyers or sellers more control.

GBPUSD — The 1.3400 area is the first barometer

item.title: What is the distribution of forecasts for the US NFP?
item.description:
The ranges of estimates are important in terms of market reaction because when the actual data deviates from the expectations, it creates a surprise effect. Another important input in market's reaction is the distribution of forecasts.

In fact, although we can have a range of estimates, most forecasts might be clustered on the upper bound of the range, so even if the data comes out inside the range of estimates but on the lower bound of the range, it can still create a surprise effect.

Non-Farm Payrolls

  • 35K to 125K range of estimates
  • 50K-75K range most clustered
  • 65K consensus

Unemployment Rate

  • 4.3% (8%)
  • 4.2% (74%) - consensus
  • 4.1% (18%)

Average Hourly Earnings Y/Y

  • 3.0% (14%)
  • 2.9% (66%) - consensus
  • 2.8% (20%)

Average Hourly Earnings M/M

  • 0.4% (7%)
  • 0.3% (72%) - consensus
  • 0.2% (21%)

The reaction to data is going to be tricky because there could be something for everyone today. A bad report could strengthen growth concerns and extend the risk-off sentiment. At the same time, it could also lead to a dovish repricing in interest rate expectations and support risk assets on a less hawkish Fed. In the current context, I would say the former is more probable.

The same goes for a good report. In this case, we might see a hawkish repricing that could weigh further on risk assets. But, good data could also trigger a relief rally on easing growth concerns. I guess the market would like to see good data, just not too hot.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

It's been a relatively quiet session, with limited news and data releases. In terms of data, the only highlight was the Eurozone retail sales report. Retail sales fell by -0.7% m/m in September, missing the -0.1% forecast, while annual growth slowed to 0.4% from 0.8%. The decline was mainly driven by non-food products, although food, drinks and tobacco sales also weakened. Germany recorded the largest monthly drop, with sales falling 2.0%.

The data points to weakening consumer demand amid elevated energy prices and higher interest rates. However, the data doesn't change the ECB's policy outlook, as the central bank remains primarily focused on inflation.

Fed's Williams described the US economy as remarkably resilient, with stronger growth and a stable labour market. He noted that tariff-related inflation pressures have largely passed through, energy costs are evolving as expected, and longer-term inflation expectations remain anchored, with wage growth consistent with the Fed’s 2% target. Williams seems comfortable with the current economic backdrop and sees no urgency to adjust interest rates, favouring a wait-and-see approach as the Fed assesses incoming data.

The Deputy Head of Iran's top security body told state TV that it remains sceptical of US diplomatic commitments, insisting that written assurances are not enough and that Washington must take concrete steps before negotiations can resume. Iran is demanding practical evidence of US intentions rather than relying on promises. It looks like Iran is trying to capitalise on the US midterms results and wants the US to agree on all its terms. There's a risk that it could force Trump to order renewed military operations now that he has nothing to lose.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: Zcash resists crypto market selloff as network upgrade goes live. What's next?
item.description:
Zcash showed notable resilience yesterday amid the rout in the crypto market. The NU7 network upgrade might have provided some support. As a reminder, the upgrade reduces block times from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, making payments three times faster.

It will also disable older Sprout transaction pools and introduce a Network Sustainability Mechanism aimed at supporting the network's long-term funding. This is an important milestone for Zcash's development.

Nevertheless, the macro headwinds will continue to limit the upside. The Democratic Congress is expected to limit fiscal expansion and bring tighter regulation and restriction on AI infrastructure. Since the US economy is leveraged to AI investment, it could lead to a slowdown in growth and weigh on risk sentiment.

The wild card is the US-Iran situation. A breakthrough in negotiations would be positive for Zcash on improving growth outlook and risk sentiment. An escalation, on the other hand, will likely trigger another selloff on increasing growth concerns and safe haven flows, although there’s a chance that it could be short-lived if Trump launches limited strikes just to save face before exiting the war.

 

ZCASH TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME

On the daily chart, we can see that Zcashis approaching the major resistance zone around the 1,380 level. If the price gets there, we can expect the sellers to step in, with a defined risk above the resistance, to position for a drop into the 1,031 support. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to increase the bullish bets into the 1,692 level next.

ZCASH TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – 4 HOUR TIMEFRAME

On the 4 hour chart, we have an upward trendline defining the bullish momentum into the resistance. The buyers will likely continue to lean on the trendline, with a defined risk below it, to keep pushing into new highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break lower to pile in for a drop into the 1,031 support next.

On the 1 hour chart, there’s not much we can add here as the buyers will continue to lean on the trendline to target new highs, while the sellers will wait for a break below the trendline or a rally into the resistance to position for new lows. The red lines define the average daily range for today.

item.title: US-Iran uncertainty keeps the downside in oil limited as markets await further developments
item.description:
Crude oil trimmed some losses yesterday as the market seems to have realised that Trump can still legally continue military operations against Iran even if Democrats control Congress.

The US-Iran situation remains mostly unchanged. Trump said that he has to decide whether to take further action against Tehran, while adding that he would prefer not to destroy the rest of Iran.

According to Axios, Trump met with his national security team before making the comments, while CENTCOM is reportedly finalising preparations for potentially resuming major combat operations. However, no new directive has been issued.

Meanwhile, the diplomatic efforts continue. Iran reportedly submitted a new nuclear proposal to the US through Qatar, but a senior Iranian official said Tehran would only discuss it once Washington meets its seven demands. Fars News also reported that Iran does not envisage further diplomatic steps until their conditions are met.

The New York Times reported that Iran is reviewing proposals from mediators concerning its nuclear programme, with Vice President Vance reportedly emerging as a key supporter of Qatar-led mediation efforts.

Nevertheless, US military strikes remain an option as Trump could consider limited strikes against Iranian nuclear facilities rather than broader attacks on energy infrastructure.

Looking ahead, the focus will remain on US-Iran developments. A breakthrough would increase the bearish momentum significantly and take oil prices back to pre-war levels relatively quickly. An escalation, on the other hand, could trigger another rally on a rising risk premium, although there’s also a chance that it could be short-lived if Trump launches limited strikes just to save face before exiting the war. 

 

CRUDE OIL TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME

On the daily chart, we can see that crude oil(CFD contract) extended the gains after bouncing from the key 87.00 handle. The broken channel could act as resistance in case the price retests the bottom trendline. We can expect the sellers to step in around the broken trendline, with a defined risk above it, to target a drop below the 87.00 handle, targeting the 80.00 level. The buyers, on the other hand, will want to see the price breaking higher to increase the bullish bets into the 110.00 resistance next.

On the 4 hour chart, we have a downward trendline defining the bearish momentum. We haven’t got neither a rejection nor a clean breakout, so it became useless. If we get another pullback into the 87.00 handle, we can expect the buyers to step in around that level, with a defined risk below it, to keep targeting the 110.00 resistance. The sellers, on the other hand, will look for a break lower to increase the bearish bets into the 80.00 handle next.

The buyers stepped in around the support, with a defined risk below it, to keep pushing into new highs. The sellers will want to see the price breaking lower to position for a drop below the 87.00 level next. The red lines define the average daily range for today.

item.title: Eurozone retail sales fall 0.7% in September, signalling weakening consumer demand
item.description:
• Retail sales m/m -0.7% vs -0.1% expected
  • Prior +0.1%
  • Retail sales y/y +0.4% vs +0.6% expected
  • Prior +0.8%
  • Full report

Eurozone retail sales declined more than expected in September, falling 0.7% m/m. Germany recorded the largest monthly decline, with retail sales falling 2.0%. The EU-wide figure also weakened, dropping 0.6% m/m. The decline was primarily driven by non-food products, where sales volumes dropped 1.2% in the euro area and 1.0% across the EU. Food, drinks and tobacco sales also weakened, falling 0.3% and 0.4%, respectively. Automotive fuel was the only category to record an increase, rising 1.0% in the euro area and 0.1% in the EU.

On an annual basis, however, retail trade volumes remained positive, increasing by 0.4% y/y in the euro area and 0.9% in the EU, although the data still missed expectations. Within the euro area, food, drinks and tobacco recorded the strongest annual growth at 1.1%, followed by non-food products at 0.7%. Automotive fuel sales remained under pressure, declining 3.0% y/y.

The September figures point to weakening consumer demand amid higher interest rates and elevated energy prices. The Retail Sales report is almost never a market-moving release and the data doesn't change anything for the ECB as the central bank remains focused on inflation.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

It looks like the market realised that the blue sweep is not a good thing amid more fiscal restraint and tighter regulation and restrictions on AI infrastructure.

Moreover, a Democratic Congress doesn’t limit Trump’s power to impose tariffs or continue the war with Iran. So, all in all, this should be a net negative for the growth outlook and therefore for risk sentiment, unless the US-Iran war finally ends.

Looking ahead, the focus will remain on US-Iran developments and the Fed. A breakthrough ion negotiations would be positive for Bitcoin on improving growth outlook and positive risk sentiment. An escalation, on the other hand, will likely trigger another selloff on increasing growth concerns and safe haven flows.

item.title: Fed's Williams says US economy remains resilient, appropriate time to gather more information
item.description:
• US economy remarkably resilient
  • Growth has strengthened
  • US facing unusual supply and demand shocks
  • Remarkably stable and solid labour market
  • We've seen tariffs effect work way through, mostly behind us
  • Energy passing through to inflation as expected
  • Inflation expectations well anchored
  • Wage growth consistent with 2% goal
  • This is appropriate time to gather more info

New York Fed President John Williams highlighted the resilience of the US economy while signalling that the Federal Reserve can afford to take time to assess incoming data before making further policy decisions.

Williams said economic growth has strengthened, describing the US economy as remarkably resilient despite facing unusual demand and supply-side shocks. He also characterised the labour market as remarkably stable and solid, suggesting that employment conditions remain broadly supportive of the economic outlook.

On inflation, Williams noted that the impact of tariffs has largely worked its way through the economy and is now mostly behind us. Meanwhile, energy costs are passing through to inflation broadly as expected. He added that longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored and wage growth is consistent with the Fed's 2% inflation target.

Williams is relatively comfortable with the current economic backdrop and doesn't see the need to rush on interest rates.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: A welcome change for gold as tech selloff fails to spark heavy liquidation, breaking the recent pattern
item.description:
Gold came under some pressure yesterday amid the tech stocks rout. The good news is that we haven’t experienced the same strong liquidation that we’ve seen in the past weeks.

This might be due to the change in context and positioning. We now have a Democratic Congress which is going to restrain fiscal expansion and likely limit the rise in Treasury yields. At the same time, we still have the war in Iran that is likely to keep inflation expectations high.

The result is lower real yields, especially with the rout in tech stocks weighing on growth expectations and nominal yields.

The positioning in gold is also much less crowded than at the start of the year. BofA's FMS survey had already shown in July that gold was the most undervalued since 2023, which should provide further support for the precious metal.

The focus will now be on the US-Iran situation and the Fed. If Trump decides to escalate the war, inflation expectations would rise alongside weakening growth outlook, creating a stagflationary environment. This is bullish for gold.

At the same time, if we get a de-escalation, we could see a dovish repricing on easing inflation concerns, which could also support gold in the short-term.

Today, we have the US NFP report. Soft data could lower rate hike probabilities further and trigger a rally in gold. A hot report, on the other hand, is unlikely to change much for the Fed, so a downward spike could be quickly faded.

 

GOLD TECHNICAL ANALYSIS – DAILY TIMEFRAME

On the daily chart, we can see that gold(CFD contract) broke above the key downward trendline and pulled back to retest it. The buyers will likely continue to pile in around these levels, with a defined risk below the trendline, to keep targeting new highs. The sellers, on the other hand, will need to see the price breaking below the major upward trendline to open the door for new lows.

item.title: Newmont stock breaks out of a two-month downtrend. But buyers have a test to pass.
item.description:
Gold and other precious metals are showing signs of a potentially significant bullish reversal.

But not every investor wants to trade physical gold, futures or other metal-linked instruments.

One stock worth watching is Newmont Corporation (NYSE: NEM), a major gold producer. Its four-hour chart shows a promising technical development, although the most useful part of this analysis is not a prediction. It's the price map that can help us assess whether the breakout succeeds or fails.

I'm not recommending that readers buy Newmont. Technical patterns can fail, and even a strong rally in gold does not guarantee that gold-mining shares will follow.

A downtrend that may have turned into a bull flag

As discussed in investingLive's recent gold technical analysis, gold has broken above an important declining trendline, raising the possibility of a broader recovery.

Newmont's four-hour chart presents an interesting parallel.

Since early September, NEM has traded inside a descending channel, repeatedly making lower highs and generally struggling to maintain rallies.

But after declining toward $104.50 in late October, the stock recovered sharply, breaking above the channel's upper boundary and advancing toward $122-$123.

That changes the technical interpretation.

What previously looked like a persistent downtrend may prove to have been a bull flag, a downward-sloping consolidation that can interrupt a larger bullish move before the advance resumes.

The important distinction is that a breakout does not guarantee the pattern will work. Buyers still need to demonstrate that they can defend the recovery.

Why $117-$118 may be the most interesting area on the chart

The chart reveals something particularly useful.

Newmont has pulled back toward the $117-$118 area, which coincides with the Point of Control (PoC) of the recent trading range.

For readers unfamiliar with the term, the Point of Control represents the price level where the greatest amount of volume was traded over a selected period.

It can become an important reference point because considerable trading activity previously occurred there. However, that does not automatically make it support.

For Newmont, the question is whether the recent breakout has changed market behavior sufficiently for buyers to defend this area.

A successful retest could strengthen the bullish interpretation. A sustained move below it would indicate that the recovery is losing momentum.

The stock also faces resistance around $120, making the nearby price structure particularly interesting.

The Newmont stock price map: What would strengthen or weaken the bullish case?

Rather than assuming that the breakout means Newmont is heading higher, I would focus on three possible developments.

1. Bullish continuation: Above $120, then $122-$123

If NEM establishes sustained trading above $120 and subsequently clears the $122-$123 resistance area, the bullish case would improve.

That could bring the September high around $130.75 back into focus.

It would not guarantee a move toward that level, but it would indicate that buyers have overcome another important obstacle.

2. Constructive pullback: Holding $117-$118

A pullback that stabilizes around $117-$118, particularly if followed by a higher low and renewed buying, could provide evidence that the recent breakout is holding.

This would be constructive even without an immediate rally.

In fact, watching how a market behaves after an initial breakout can sometimes be more informative than watching the breakout itself.

3. Failed breakout: Below approximately $115

Sustained trading below $115 would materially weaken the emerging bullish structure.

Attention could then shift toward the $112 support area. Further deterioration could eventually put the November low around $104.50 back into focus.

That would suggest the apparent bull flag breakout had failed, rather than developed into a sustained bullish continuation.

Gold exposure through a stock is different from owning gold

There is another important distinction for investors.

Newmont is a mining company, not a direct substitute for bullion. Its share price reflects gold prices, but also production volumes, operating costs, capital spending and broader equity-market conditions.

In its third-quarter 2026 results, Newmont reported approximately 1.3 million attributable ounces of gold production and $1.9 billion in free cash flow. The company also maintained its full-year production outlook while improving its full-year cost guidance.

Those fundamentals may matter to investors assessing the company beyond the chart, but they do not eliminate mining-specific risks.

A recovering gold price can benefit producers, yet Newmont shares can still underperform if costs rise, production disappoints or equity markets come under pressure.

The lesson: A good map is more valuable than a confident prediction

What interests me most about Newmont is not simply that it has broken above a descending channel.

It's that the chart now provides several identifiable reference areas against which we can evaluate the bullish hypothesis.

The $117-$118 area may help reveal whether buyers are defending the breakout. A recovery above $120 and $122-$123 would strengthen the continuation case. A sustained decline below $115 would challenge it.

We don't need to know in advance which outcome will occur to make the analysis useful.

For investors exploring possible exposure to a precious-metals recovery through listed companies, Newmont is an interesting stock to investigate further.

But a potential bull flag is not a reason to buy automatically. Its value lies in understanding what would confirm the opportunity, what would undermine it and when patience may be the better decision.

What else is interesting for traders and investors today?

Following a punishing tech rout that saw Nasdaq-100 futures plunge 5,250 points (Almost 17%...!) from their October high, I am tracking whether buyers can turn an initial 800-point bounce off historical support into something more durable. As I broke down in my Nasdaq technical analysis after yesterday's crash, the 26,350–26,400 zone provided an immediate reaction, but my tradeCompass framework demands sustained trading above 27,200 to validate a constructive bullish continuation, otherwise, slipping below 26,850 risks reopening downside exposure.

This fragile stabilization comes as regional bourses absorb heavy selling, detailed in the investingLive Asia-Pacific news wrap on global tech rout growth concerns, where heavy pressure on chip and data-center supply chains spilled across Asian equity sessions.

Macro and geopolitical crosscurrents continue to dictate intraday positioning, with Adam Button at investingLive.com noting that the market is waiting for critical policy signals from Donald Trump regarding post-midterm tariff strategy and Middle East tensions, leaving risk assets caught between relief rallies and supply-side uncertainties.

Traders now turn their focus to high-impact economic catalysts to close out the week; as Giuseppe Dellamotta outlined when previewing the main economic events on today's calendar, session volatility is poised to spike with the release of the U.S. non-farm payrolls (NFP) report, Canadian employment data, and the preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey.

Educational market analysis only. Not a recommendation to buy or sell. Trade at your own risk.

This article was written by Itai Levitan at investinglive.com.

item.title: investingLive Asia-pacific news wrap: Global tech stocks rout raises growth concerns
item.description:
US Democrats are reportedly targeting President Trump's tariffs on Canada as the first step towards rolling back parts of his administration's trade policy. Meanwhile, BoC Governor Macklem said he remains optimistic about lower US tariffs but cannot rule out further escalation before trade conditions improve.

President Trump, in a Truth Social post, acknowledged the sharp equity market sell-off, saying stocks had suffered one of their worst days ever but would ultimately become bigger and stronger.

War Secretary Hegseth could reportedly face an impeachment vote as soon as next week. Secretary of State Rubio denied reports that he was considering leaving the administration, saying he intended to remain until the end of Trump's term.

Texas Governor-elect said data centre development should be halted until measures are introduced to protect residents.

The US-Iran situation remained mostly unchanged, with President Trump saying Washington needed to decide whether to take further action against Tehran, while adding that he would prefer not to destroy the rest of Iran.

According to Axios, Trump met with his national security team before making the comments, while CENTCOM is reportedly finalising preparations for potentially resuming major combat operations. However, no new directive has been issued.

Diplomatic efforts continue. Iran reportedly submitted a new nuclear proposal to the US through Qatar, but a senior Iranian official said Tehran would only discuss it once Washington meets its seven demands. Fars News also reported that Iran does not envisage further diplomatic steps until those conditions are met.

The NYT reported that Iran is reviewing concrete proposals from mediators concerning its nuclear programme, with Vice President Vance reportedly emerging as a key supporter of Qatar-led mediation efforts.

Nevertheless, US military strikes remain an option, with reports suggesting Trump could consider limited strikes against Iranian nuclear facilities rather than broader attacks on energy infrastructure.

Asian governments signalled their readiness to respond to heightened financial market volatility following the global equity sell-off. South Korea's finance minister said authorities would take necessary measures to prevent excessive market reactions and significant deviations from fundamentals. The government also announced a three-month easing of margin requirements.

Taiwan ordered regulators to closely monitor equity markets and prepare flexible stabilisation measures. Meanwhile, Japanese PM Takaichi said the government was considering support payments for more than 30% of workers.

In Canada, the government proposed total borrowing of CAD 611bln for 2027/28, up from CAD 587bln in 2026/27. However, deficit projections were revised lower across the forecast horizon. The government also lowered its GDP growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027.

Looking ahead, the focus will remain on the fallout from the US midterm elections and the developments in the US-Iran war. 

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

What are FX option expiries?

The FX option expiration price levels refer to the strike prices where option contracts are set to expire. These levels include both calls and puts.

When you see "EUR/USD at 1.1600 for €4 billion" it means there is a total of €4 billion worth of options (calls + puts combined) that have a strike price of 1.1600 and are expiring at that specific time (the "New York Cut" at 10:00 AM ET).

Traders watch these levels because they often act as a "magnet" for the price. For example, if there's nothing happening in the market and the price is close to the expiry level, let's say 30-50 pips away, what you will usually see is the price moving into the expiry level. This happens due to the hedging activity of the market makers (banks, dealers and so on).

As the price gets closer to the strike price near expiration, these market makers must aggressively buy or sell the currency to hedge their risk. This hedging activity tends to suppress volatility and keep the price "pinned" close to the strike price until the expiration time passes.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

item.title: What are the main events for today?
item.description:
EUROPEAN SESSION

In the European session, we don't have much on the agenda other that a couple of low-tier releases like the Swiss consumer confidence and the Eurozone retail sales. The data won't change anything for the respective central banks, so the market reaction will be muted. 

The focus remains on the fallout from the US midterm elections and the US-Iran situation. The rout in tech stocks has weighed on growth expectations, putting pressure on Treasury yields and rate hike expectations. The probabilities for a December Fed rate hike fell to 67%, from roughly 80% earlier in the week. 

AMERICAN SESSION

In the American session, we get the US NFP report, the Canadian employment data and the University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey. The NFP is expected at 65K vs 29K, with the unemployment rate remaining unchanged at 4.2%. The Average Hourly Earnings Y/Y is expected at 2.9% vs 3.0% prior, while the M/M measure is seen at 0.3% vs 0.1% prior. 

The reaction to data is going to be tricky because there could be something for everyone. A bad report could strengthen growth concerns and extend the risk-off sentiment. At the same time, it could also lead to a dovish repricing in interest rate expectations and support risk assets on a less hawkish Fed. In the current context, I would say the former is more probable.

The same goes for a good report. In this case, we might see a hawkish repricing that could weigh further on risk assets. But, good data could also trigger a relief rally on easing growth concerns. I guess the market would like to see good data, just not too hot. 

The Canadian employment change is expected at 13.6K vs -68.3K prior, with the unemployment rate remaining unchanged at 6.8%. The market is pricing just a 38% chance of a BoC rate hike in December, so we will likely need a very strong report followed by hot inflation data to raise the probabilities. I personally think the BoC shouldn't have hiked based on the data as labour market conditions has been soft and underlying inflation has held around the 2% target. A global rout in stock markets would just add downward pressure on economic activity. 

The University of Michigan consumer sentiment is expected at 48.0 vs 46.7 prior. We could see a minor rebound in the sentiment after the drop in gasoline prices, but I don't expect the data to matter much at this point.

item.title: Nasdaq analysis after yesterday's crash: Is this the dip investors have been waiting for?
item.description:
Nasdaq futures rebound after a 16.6% plunge. Is this a dip to buy or a rally to sell?

Nasdaq futures have bounced nearly 800 points from a major historical support zone, but Wall Street's earnings mood remains defensive. With another important economic report approaching, Friday could provide a crucial test of whether buyers are returning or the bearish trend is simply taking a break.

November 6, 2026 | Nasdaq-100 E-mini Futures (NQ)

Nasdaq-100 futures have fallen 5,250 points, or 16.61%, from their October high in just 23 trading sessions. Yet the latest decline has brought NQ into a particularly interesting support zone around 26,350-26,400, where buyers have finally responded.

Is this a dip worth buying? Possibly. But the price recovery, while impressive, remains unconfirmed, and the broader earnings environment gives me reasons to remain cautious.

The Nasdaq selloff has been brutal, but the latest low is interesting

Thursday's session delivered another reminder of how quickly market sentiment can change.

The cash Nasdaq-100 index declined 6.36%, its worst single-day performance since 2020, with selling particularly severe across artificial intelligence, semiconductors and data-center infrastructure companies.

As investingLive reported in its review of the Nasdaq-100 selloff, the pressure extended well beyond a handful of high-profile technology stocks.

The decline was also visible in the broader market. European trading saw US technology and chip liquidation intensify, although European equity markets themselves delivered a more mixed performance.

But while the headlines describe a market under considerable pressure, the futures chart offers another perspective.

From an October high of 31,616.50, Nasdaq futures have declined to 26,366.50 in the latest overnight session.

That is a decline of exactly 5,250 points, or approximately 16.61%.

And the location of that low matters.

Why 26,350-26,400 is more than just another support level

The longer-term futures chart identifies two previous major highs:

  • 26,399: An important historical high.

  • 26,349: Another major historical high.

  • 26,366.50: The latest low reached during the selloff.

These three prices are clustered within just 50 points of each other.

When markets break above previous highs, those former resistance areas can sometimes become support during subsequent corrections.

The logic is straightforward: a price area where sellers previously stopped an advance may later attract buying when the market returns from above.

That does not always happen, of course.

But in this case, the response has been encouraging. Nasdaq futures rebounded to approximately 27,159, recovering nearly 793 points from their latest low.

For traders watching for signs of a possible bottom, this is an important development.

Still, I would distinguish between a successful initial defense of support and a confirmed reversal of the wider downtrend.

The futures market has recovered only about 15% of the preceding 5,250-point decline. There is still considerable technical damage to repair.

Earnings season offers another warning: Investors are becoming selective

I also think we should look beyond the Nasdaq chart to understand what may happen next.

The latest earnings season has been notably defensive.

In a provisional review of 337 companies with usable earnings-reaction data through November 5, approximately 35.3% recorded positive reactions. The equal-weighted average reaction was around -3.59%, compared with approximately -1.23% on a market-capitalization-weighted basis.

These are preliminary estimates based on mixed-source observations, not a complete census of final earnings returns. Nevertheless, the imbalance is worth monitoring.

It suggests that investors have been more inclined to punish disappointing reports than to reward companies broadly.

But the most recent earnings announcements also reveal an interesting exception.

In the latest available after-hours observations:

  • Airbnb (ABNB): Up approximately 11.0% following earnings.

  • Cloudflare (NET): Up approximately 14.1%.

  • DraftKings (DKNG): Down approximately 21.7%.

  • Atlassian (TEAM): Down approximately 16.5%.

These are provisional extended-hours reactions measured against their respective pre-earnings regular-session references, not completed Friday returns.

What interests me here is the contrast.

Investors are clearly still willing to reward individual companies, sometimes quite aggressively. However, the differences between winners and losers remain extreme.

Earlier in the week, initial positive reactions in companies such as AMD and Arista Networks also struggled to retain their gains.

That creates an additional question for Friday: Will the latest earnings winners retain their gains when regular trading begins, or will renewed selling pressure overwhelm them?

For Nasdaq traders, this matters because a more sustainable index rebound would be more convincing if it were accompanied by improving technology-sector participation and stronger follow-through after earnings.

These individual earnings reactions are evidence of market selectivity, not a calculation of their contribution to NQ futures.

The AI trade is also facing a different question

The market is reconsidering the economics of the enormous AI infrastructure buildout.

Interestingly, as Adam Button discussed in why markets might welcome a slower data-center expansion, reduced capital spending could actually benefit some of the largest technology platforms by improving free cash flow.

That creates an important distinction between companies spending heavily on AI infrastructure and those supplying the chips, equipment, power and construction capacity.

A slower buildout might help the finances of some hyperscalers while hurting demand expectations for some of their suppliers.

The market is not necessarily abandoning AI. It may be questioning the timing, scale and financial returns of the investment cycle.

For Nasdaq investors, this distinction could become increasingly important over the coming months.

Friday's Nasdaq tradeCompass: Two important activation levels

Turning back to the futures chart, my directional assessment remains -5 on a scale from -10 to +10, reflecting a bearish broader structure despite the developing rebound.

However, that assessment is not a prediction that Friday must be a negative session.

The following tradeCompass scenarios provide conditional reference points based on the latest available 30-minute futures chart.

Bullish scenario: Above 27,200

Buyers have encountered resistance around 27,135-27,160 during the latest recovery.

I would prefer to see NQ establish sustained trading above 27,200 before treating the rebound as a stronger intraday bullish opportunity.

A brief move through the level would not necessarily be sufficient. Ideally, buyers would demonstrate that they can hold recovered ground when sellers return.

Potential bullish partial profit targets:

The second target is particularly interesting because it is positioned just beneath a previous value-area resistance boundary around 27,488.50.

A successful recovery above this region would represent a more meaningful improvement in the short-term technical structure.

Conversely, if NQ breaks above 27,200 but quickly returns below the nearby recovery area, the bullish scenario would lose credibility.

Importantly, a recovery toward these targets would still not automatically confirm that the larger correction has ended.

Bearish scenario: Below 26,850

The bearish scenario becomes more attractive if sellers regain control and NQ establishes sustained trading below 26,850.

That would indicate a deterioration in the recovery structure and a loss of the nearby support concentration around 26,880.

Potential bearish partial profit targets:

TP4 is conditional on a decisive breakdown below the 26,350-26,400 historical support zone.

This distinction matters.

The area around 26,350-26,400 has already attracted meaningful buying interest. I would not assume that sellers can simply push through it without another contest.

The third bearish target, at 26,415, is therefore positioned ahead of that historical support region.

A sustained recovery above 27,200 would weaken the immediate bearish-reversal thesis and call for reassessment.

What about the area between 26,850 and 27,200?

For me, this is primarily a decision zone.

Nasdaq futures can remain inside this region without generating a sufficiently strong directional opportunity.

One alternative worth monitoring is a recovery toward 27,135-27,200 that fails to hold.

Such a rejection might provide a more attractive location for traders looking to sell a rally rather than chase the market lower after an already substantial decline.

But there must be evidence of rejection. Reaching resistance alone does not establish a short trade.

Equally, a trader considering a long should not assume that simply bouncing off historical support guarantees another advance.

Friday's US jobs report could change the picture quickly

There is another important consideration for November 6.

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics employment report for October is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time, one hour before the US stock market opens.

That could have an important influence on Nasdaq futures.

A report that materially changes expectations for Federal Reserve policy, inflation or economic growth could produce substantial volatility.

For example, weaker employment data might encourage expectations of easier monetary policy, but an unexpectedly severe deterioration could simultaneously raise concerns about future corporate earnings.

Likewise, stronger employment figures might support confidence in economic growth while potentially making interest-rate relief less likely.

The market's interpretation, not simply whether the number is above or below expectations, will matter.

That makes it especially important to reassess the futures map if the announcement produces a substantial price adjustment.

Meanwhile, political and geopolitical uncertainty remains another source of potential market volatility.

As Adam Button discussed in the market's search for signals from Donald Trump, investors are assessing whether the administration responds to the midterm election results by changing course or maintaining its existing approach to trade and foreign policy.

Energy markets add another dimension. The recent decline in refining margins and signs of potential normalization could eventually matter for fuel prices and inflation expectations, although significant energy-supply risks remain.

These developments should not automatically be treated as explanations for every Nasdaq price movement. They are additional variables that traders need to consider when interpreting the next move.

Is the Nasdaq dip an opportunity for longer-term investors?

I believe the 26,350-26,400 support cluster deserves attention beyond Friday's trading session.

For an investor looking to increase technology exposure after a substantial correction, a return to important historical price levels may offer an opportunity to evaluate potential entries.

But a lower price is not necessarily a better investment.

The latest earnings season illustrates why.

Some companies are experiencing considerable changes in their growth outlook, spending requirements and investor expectations. Others are still reporting results strong enough to attract substantial buying interest.

A longer-term investor should consider whether a company's earnings outlook, valuation and competitive position remain attractive, rather than relying exclusively on an index-level support zone.

For the Nasdaq as a whole, I would become more constructive if the historical support cluster continues to hold and the market begins establishing a sequence of higher lows and recovering important resistance areas.

If the cluster breaks decisively, however, the possibility of a deeper correction would require renewed consideration.

My Nasdaq outlook for Friday

There are two opposing developments worth respecting.

First, the broader technical structure remains bearish after a 16.61% correction. The weakness in earnings reactions, together with uncertainty surrounding the AI investment cycle, gives little reason to assume that the selling pressure has disappeared.

Second, Nasdaq futures have reached a historically meaningful support cluster and produced a substantial initial recovery.

That deserves attention too.

For Friday's day traders, 27,200 is the bullish activation level, while 26,850 is the bearish activation level.

For swing traders and investors, the more consequential reference remains 26,350-26,400.

I would be especially interested in whether buyers can sustain the recovery after the US employment report and into the regular trading session.

A successful defense, improving earnings follow-through and a recovery through successive resistance levels would strengthen the argument that the latest Nasdaq dip is becoming an opportunity.

A failed rebound, renewed selling across technology stocks and a decisive loss of historical support would argue otherwise.

My broader directional lean remains bearish, but the rebound has changed the short-term risk-reward picture. After such an extended decline, chasing shorts into major support deserves particular caution.

For traders using the tradeCompass approach, the objective remains to respond to evidence rather than predict every move. Consider partial profits at planned targets, size positions around a defined invalidation point and remember that doing nothing is sometimes the most sensible decision.
